cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've borrowed five thousand for the charity auction advance. Record it as a commitment, not a shortfall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only your mum registered, and she's just giving us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll bid. A commitment must be honoured; separate that from attendance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If we borrow more to buy our own prizes, we'll owe both loans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put both loans under liabilities. The donation still belongs under charitable giving. Now raise the limit; I cannot enter a bid you won't fund.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commitment classification and A5 liability/donation columns turn A disaster-selling into a supposedly expert accounting exercise.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no bidders causes A3 self-bidding; B4 two loans is acknowledged in A5 rather than falsely corrected.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 have accurate practical objections; A reframes them to keep the scheme going.

heightening.evidence: A5 absorbs the extra debt into the sheet and makes further funding the partner obligation.

specificity.evidence: A1 borrowed charity advance and B4 second loan make the financial trap understandable.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 column distinctions are used to obtain funding, though the three-clause ending remains fuller than ideal.
